## 🔖 Book Summary

Sophie is just a normal, ordinary eldest daughter in a hat shop. One day, she got cursed by the Witch of the Waste and turned into an old lady. On her journey to find a way to change back into her younger self, she found herself love, friendship, her gift of magic and her confidence. On that journey, she met Howl, an infamous wizard in the land, who is known as the man who eats young girls’ hearts and souls. Yet, he actually just is an ordinary man, living in Wales with his sister’s family, possesses a great gift of magic. Together, they defeated the Witch of the Waste and found their happily ever after.



## 🔖 Book Review


## ✨Overview:
**(theme, genre, first feeling, mood board, keywords)**

At first, I was quite surprised to know that the characters in this novel are very different from the animated movie of Ghibli. While in Ghibli movie, Howl and Sophie are much gentler, more loving, they are fierce as fire in the novel. They argue all the time, from small things to huge problems, but somehow that gives the old-married-couple vibe. They are much funnier in the book than in the movie. I read that some people said that the movie is told through Howl’s point of view and the book is told through Sophie’s perspective and I couldn’t agree more.


## ✨Plot:

**(storyline, development, pacing, specific moments, ending, plot holes, worldbuilding)**

They are really logical and surprising, exciting along with relaxing. I love that Diane has built a really unique magical world that links to our normal just through a door of Howl’s castle. Every details are explained thoroughly and I don’t think there are any plot holes. However, this is just my opinion after my first reading, and I can’t guarantee that I understand all of the details in this book. Some of them are quite confusing to me, it’s a whole new concept after all.

## ✨Characters:

**(main and favorite characters - development, personality, why like, ending)**

The characters’ developments and the plot are much deeper than in the movie, and much more diverse.

**Sophie:** at first she’s just a shy girl, who thinks herself as a failure just because she’s an eldest child. She was called as ‘mouse’ in the first few chapters since she’s scared easily and do not like crowded places or people. Somehow, she can calmly accept that herself just turned into a ninety-year-old lady, without throwing any tantrum (which will happens in later chapters). Then, throughout the story, she started to show more of herself, regain her confidence and be more sure of herself. Surprisingly, she has a gift of magic, through her words and sayings. This detail is amazing actually, it makes more sense than in the movie where she helps Howl just by loving him. I love that she has a fierce personality just like the colour of her hair.

**Howl:** Oh, he is a drama queen. He throws tantrum over small things like his hair and his clothes. He’s a coward, but deep inside, he is a brave soul. I love that he tried to tricked himself into being brave by actively slithering out of things and calling himself a wicked coward. And just like the movie, he also has a tender heart and a kind soul, saving Calcifer just because he pitied him, trying to save Sophie and himself, unconsciously and consciously loving Sophie with all his being. Overall, Howl still has a little bit of the movie’s personality, just more dramatic and less romantic. Though I think he’s more lively and funny in the book, not someone I would want to marry but still an interesting man, which is really different from his perfect dreamy version in the animated movie.

**Other characters:** They all have some slight differences to huge ones from the movie. From the character Martha and her love story with Michael, the brave Lettie, the encouraging and kind Fanny-stepmother, Prince Justin and Wizard Sulliman are really different from the movie too.

## ✨Prose:

**(author’s + translator’s writing style)**

I think Diane’s writing style is a little bit old-fashioned to me, and too theatre-like. I found some of the sentences are too formal or too hard to understand. However, they are still quite enjoyable.
